title: Sodium bicarbonate and sodium chloride: effects on blood pressure and electrolyte homeostasis in normal and hypertensive man
authors: Luft FC, Zemel MB, Sowers JA, Fineberg NS, Weinberger MH
followUp: 7 days on each regimen, crossover one month apart
population: 10 mildly hypertensive and 10 normotensive adults on a fixed basal diet of 60 mmol sodium and chloride, 60 mmol potassium and 14 mmol calcium a day
funder: Not read: the publisher offers the article only as a subscriber PDF. PubMed lists grant RR 00750 (NCRR, NIH) and the publication types Research Support, U.S. Gov't, P.H.S. and Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't.
result: Randomly allocated, placebo-controlled crossover trial. After 4 days of balance, participants drank 3 L/day of a NaHCO3-containing mineral water (26.2 mmol/L sodium, 33.03 mmol/L HCO3) or a control solution with equimolar cations as chloride salts for 7 days (total sodium 138 mmol/day). NaCl did not influence blood pressure, whereas NaHCO3 decreased systolic blood pressure by 5 mmHg in the hypertensive subjects. Both regimens decreased plasma renin activity in the hypertensive subjects. Urinary calcium excretion increased consistently with NaCl but not with NaHCO3; urate excretion was not influenced.
